  WHY: x-ai_grok-4_20 considered this a regression because legitimate zero-total entries may be valid in some convergence cases, while other reviewers described the change as an intentional fail-closed fix.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:88-91 | confidence=3

  WHY: The stop condition now looks for `PR comment audit:` as a hard boundary, and the fallback regex only strips bullet-starting `editor failed` lines, so future malformed summaries may not be handled safely.

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh: lines 133-142 (the regex capture block and subsequent arithmetic) | confidence=4
  Problem: Captured count variables (t/a/aa/ig) are not validated as numeric before `$(( ))` arithmetic; the parser only checks for non-empty after extraction.
  Why it fails at runtime: A malformed audit line (e.g. from a future editor summary containing text that partially matches a regex but yields non-digits) would cause shell arithmetic to treat the empty string as 0 silently (or error with `integer expression expected`), leading to incorrect `mismatch_found=true` decisions or false-healthy audits. The test suite only exercises well-formed fixtures.
- tests/test_validate_editor_audit.py: lines 45-57 + every test that passes `tmp_path` (14 of 16 test functions) | confidence=5
  Problem: All parameterized tests rely on `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` (via pytest `tmp_path` fixture emulation in main()), but the runner environment has no usable temp directories.
  Why it fails at runtime: `python3 tests/test_validate_editor_audit.py` now reports 15/16 tests as ERROR (FileNotFoundError for temporary directory) instead of executing the assertions. The orchestration-poll recovery sweep and review_autofix validator therefore lose their contract coverage on the shared helper. The poll contract test runs cleanly, but the audit helper coverage is broken.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh: lines 152-156 (the `if [ "${sum}" -ne "${t}" ]` block after last-run patch) | confidence=4
  Problem: Removal of the original `if [ "${t}" -gt 0 ] &&` guard now forces arithmetic comparison on every parsed line, including legitimate zero-total entries that previously bypassed.
  Why it fails at runtime: Zero-total summaries (valid in some convergence cases) will now always trigger mismatch if any count is non-zero, incorrectly setting `EDITOR_NOOP_SUSPICIOUS=true` and blocking normal auto-merge paths.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh: lines 88-91 after the latest edit | confidence=3
  Problem: The stop condition now looks for `PR comment audit:` as a hard boundary, but the regex for fallback bullets was narrowed to `^[\s]*-[\s]*editor failed`.
  Why it fails at runtime: A legitimate audit line containing the substring "editor failed" (e.g. a filename or note) is no longer stripped only when it matches the anchored bullet form; the test `test_legitimate_audit_line_containing_editor_failed_phrase_is_not_filtered` passes, but the extractor logic is fragile for future malformed summaries. The temp-file error paths (rc=3) are correctly covered but only reachable when the helper is missing.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml, .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml: the added `python3 tests/test_validate_editor_audit.py` and `test_orchestrate_poll_noop_suspicious_recovery.py` lines (most recent changes shown in last_run_diff.patch) | confidence=5
  Problem: The test files were added to the explicit allowlists, but `test_validate_editor_audit.py` is broken under the runner's tempfile restrictions.
  Why it fails at runtime: CI now runs a failing test suite for the new shared audit helper, breaking the mark-stable gate and any consumer CI that pulls @stable. The noop-suspicious recovery contract test passes cleanly.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
